issues.display_title: Issue #53: fix(map): prevent UI freeze when switching selection mode from frames to gps
issues.main_description_html:
Demo

2026-10-07.13-59-08.mp4

Summary

Fixes a severe UI freeze and lag occurring when switching coordinate selection mode from Frames to GPS.

Root Cause

When switching mode from Frames to GPS in the UI, framesStore.setSelectionMode("gps") immediately updated the manifest selection mode to "gps", while commands.computeSelection ran asynchronously in the backend. During this in-flight window:

  1. MapCanvas re-rendered immediately with isLayersMode = false.
  2. selectionResult still held the previous raw track from layers mode (~21,979 markers).
  3. getDisplayMarkers bypassed the layer frame filter (if (!isLayersMode) return valid;), dumping all raw markers into MapLibre.
  4. MapLibre attempted to instantiate ~22,000 DOM elements and SVG markers synchronously on the main thread, freezing the WebView before the new GPS selection arrived.

Solution

  1. Selection Mode Synchronization: Included mode in SelectionResult (sb-core) and SelectionResultUi (Tauri IPC), updating MapCanvas to evaluate the active mode directly from the calculated selectionResult.
  2. Defensive Safety Guard: Added a safeguard in getDisplayMarkers to prevent dumping raw tracks (>500 points and >2x frames) to the DOM during mode transitions.
  3. Tests: Added unit tests in displayMarkers.test.ts and sb-core verifying safety filtering and mode serialization.

Completed Implementation Details

  1. Selection Mode Synchronization Across IPC:

    • Updated SelectionResult in crates/sb-core/src/gps/selection.rs and SelectionResultUi in src-tauri/src/commands/projects.rs to include the computed selection mode (pub mode: SelectionMode).
    • Updated SelectionResultUi interface in src/shared/api/commands.ts.
    • Updated src/features/map/components/MapCanvas.tsx to read isLayersMode from selectionResult?.mode (falling back to manifest?.selection.mode === "layers"). This guarantees that during the asynchronous recomputation window, the UI continues displaying pins consistent with the existing computed selection result instead of prematurely switching to GPS mode and treating thousands of raw polyline samples as interactive pins.

  2. Defensive Safety Guard in getDisplayMarkers:

    • Added an automatic guard in src/features/map/model/displayMarkers.ts: if !isLayersMode is triggered while the marker list still contains raw track coordinates (valid.length > frames.length * 2 && valid.length > 500), the function automatically prevents dumping thousands of raw points to MapLibre and filters to matching selected frames instead.

  3. Testing & Quality Verification:

    • Added displayMarkers.test.ts test verifying the safety guard suppresses dumping 600 raw track markers.
    • Added Rust unit test selection_result_preserves_mode in crates/sb-core/src/gps/selection.rs.
    • Verified with:
      • cargo test --lib (139 sb-core tests + 4 app_lib tests passed)
      • cargo clippy --workspace (clean, 0 warnings)
      • Subagent rust-reviewer verification (approved: zero-cost copy, wire-compatible, safe)
      • pnpm test (16 suites, 109 unit tests passed)
      • pnpm lint (clean)
      • pnpm build (TypeScript check & Vite production build passed)

issues.display_title: Issue #52: fix(gps): resolve blueline dot cutoff by parsing true telemetry timestamps
issues.main_description_html:
demo

Summary

Fixed an issue where pin markers on the map prematurely cut off along the blue route line (only covering ~10% of the route), leaving the remainder of the route markerless.

Cause

\load_track\ in \sb-core\ previously assumed 1 sample per second (\i as f64 - 1.0). For high-frequency GPS telemetry (e.g. 10 Hz with ~21,979 points over 2,198 seconds), the video duration limit was exhausted at index 2,198, stranding the remaining 90% of the physical track.

Key Changes

  • Timestamp Parsing: Updated \load_track\ in \crates/sb-core/src/gps/selection.rs\ to parse actual elapsed seconds from \point.time\ (both float seconds and RFC 3339 timestamps), with duration interpolation fallback.
  • Full Track Coverage: Frame selection now distributes 100% across the full path (from start to end) for all step sizes.
  • EXIF Geotagging Parity: Updated \crates/sb-core/src/upload/queue.rs\ to look up frame coordinates from the computed selection result rather than linear track array indexing.

✅ Implementation & Verification Summary

Status: Completed & Ready for Review

Summary of Work Done:

  1. Telemetry Timestamp Parsing:
    • Identified root cause where \load_track\ assumed 1 sample/sec (\second = i - 1.0), cutting off 10 Hz GPS telemetry prematurely at 10% of route length.
    • Implemented \parse_point_second\ in \crates/sb-core/src/gps/selection.rs\ to accurately parse elapsed seconds from point timestamps (\point.time, both float strings and RFC 3339 timestamps) with duration interpolation fallback.
  2. 100% Track Distribution:
    • Frame selection and display markers now cover the entire track from beginning to end across all step sizes (e.g. 1 frame, 25 frames, 50 frames) along the Chobe River test track.
  3. EXIF Metadata Geotagging Fix:
    • Updated \crates/sb-core/src/upload/queue.rs\ to derive frame coordinates from selection results rather than raw array indices.
  4. Verification:
    • \cargo test --workspace\ passed (134/134 tests).
    • Golden regression tests (\golden_insta360_*) and parity hardening tests passed 100%.

issues.display_title: Issue #47: Fix Map Rendering Failure on Client Machines in Street Builder Tauri
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

Investigate and resolve an issue where the map fails to display ("still no maps visible") on the latest Tauri build when running on client machines (reported by Paul Martens / Martens Media). The issue appears to be environment-specific, as the map renders correctly in internal developer environments.

Result from Developer

Root Cause Analysis & Resolution

1. Why Did This Happen?

The issue where the map fails to display ("still no maps visible") on client machines running the packaged desktop application stems from how MapLibre GL JS v6 handles Web Workers in combination with Tauri's custom URL schemes and desktop WebViews (WebKit on macOS / WebView2 on Windows):

  1. MapLibre v6 Worker Loading Check (!url.endsWith('.cjs')):

    • In MapLibre GL v6, the internal worker factory inspects the worker URL to decide the worker instantiation mode: 
      const isModule = !url?.endsWith('.cjs');
    • When the worker was bundled as a static asset with a .js extension (e.g., maplibre-gl-worker-*.js), MapLibre flagged it as an ES Module worker and attempted to initialize it with new Worker(url, { type: 'module' }) (or via an internal import() blob wrapper when origin checks evaluated as cross-origin on custom schemes).

  2. Custom Protocol Restrictions in Production WebViews:

    • In production packaged builds, Tauri serves local assets via custom schemes:
      • macOS (WebKit / WKWebView): Uses the tauri://localhost custom scheme. WebKit restricts or refuses to spawn ES module workers across custom protocol schemes, failing asynchronously without throwing a catchable top-level exception.
      • Windows (WebView2): Under certain security configurations or Chromium versions, module workers launched via blob or cross-scheme URLs fail with Refused to cross-origin redirects of the top-level worker script.
    • As a result, the worker thread failed silently. Since MapLibre relies entirely on the Web Worker to decode PBF vector tiles, process glyphs, and generate line/polygon buckets, vector tiles never rendered (leaving only the default background color #f8f4f0 or a blank canvas with only DOM markers visible).

  3. Why It Appeared to Work in Developer Environments:

    • In pnpm tauri dev / internal dev servers, Vite serves modules over standard HTTP (http://localhost:5173). On standard HTTP origins, native ES Module workers are supported and allowed by browsers, meaning the bug only surfaced in production packages running on client devices.

2. Fix Implemented

  • Environment-Aware Worker Configuration (src/features/map/components/MapCanvas.tsx):
    • In development (import.meta.env.DEV), load the worker URL directly as an ES module to match Vite's dev server.
    • In production builds, append the #maplibre-gl-worker.cjs fragment to the bundled worker URL. This satisfies MapLibre's check and forces it to initialize as a Classic Worker (new Worker(url) without { type: 'module' }). Classic workers reliably execute the pre-bundled standalone IIFE script across all desktop webview runtimes (WebKit macOS, WebView2 Windows, and Linux).
  • Resilient Error Logging & Cleanup:
    • Wrapped new maplibregl.Map() with try / catch and registered map.on('error', ...) listeners to prevent silent failures.
    • Added proper cleanup handlers (map.off('load', ...)\) in route fitting and source updates to eliminate race conditions.

  1. Root Cause Analysis (Custom Scheme & ES Module Worker Incompatibility):
    • In packaged production desktop environments, Tauri serves web resources via custom schemes (tauri://localhost on macOS WebKit, custom origin on Windows WebView2).
    • MapLibre GL JS v6 checked worker URLs via !url.endsWith('.cjs') to decide whether to launch an ES module worker (new Worker(url, { type: 'module' })).
    • Standard desktop WebViews strictly forbid or silently reject spawning ES module workers over custom protocol schemes or cross-origin blob wrappers with Refused to cross-origin redirects of the top-level worker script.
    • Because MapLibre's background worker parses vector PBF tiles and computes render buckets, the silent worker failure left the map canvas completely blank (only showing default background color #f8f4f0).

issues.display_title: Issue #56: Fix Disabled State Validation on "Start Upload" Button in Street Builder Desktop
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-10-08.at.14.42.02.mov

Description:

Fix the disabled state logic for the "Start Upload" button in the Street Builder desktop application. While the button is expected to become enabled once both "ENTER TOUR NAME" and "ENTER TOUR ADDRESS" fields are populated, it remains disabled even after valid inputs are provided (reported by Mykola Omelchenko with Tour Name: Rivertour and Address: 54WX+XGJ, Kasane, Botswana).

Result From Developer

Root cause

The "Start Upload" button is enabled only when the tour name is non-empty and an address object is set. The address object is separate from the text shown in the address field, so the field could look filled while the address was still empty.

Ways this happened:

  1. Address typed or pasted without clicking a suggestion. While Google Maps was loaded, only a clicked suggestion set the address. Typed or pasted text was displayed but ignored. The reported value 54WX+XGJ, Kasane, Botswana is a plus code in the format Google Maps shows, which fits this path.
  2. Pressing Enter without choosing a suggestion. Google returns only the typed name in that case, and the app silently dropped it.
  3. Address lookup hanging. The backend places client had no timeout. The fallback only ran when the lookup failed, not when it hung, so on a slow connection the address never arrived.
  4. A race that wiped the address. If a save triggered by typing the tour name was still in flight when the address was picked, the returned project data overwrote the address with empty, and that empty value was then saved.
  5. Autocomplete instances piling up. A new Google Autocomplete was attached to the input on every keystroke, with no cleanup. Each one requested predictions, which risks hitting the quota and showing no suggestions.

Fix

  • Typed or pasted text is now resolved on Enter or when the field loses focus: first the top suggestion, then the Geocoder (which handles plus codes). If nothing is found, a hint appears under the field: "Address not found. Pick a suggestion from the list." (translated in all 15 locales).
  • Editing the text after picking an address clears the address, so the field and the button state can no longer disagree.
  • Autocomplete is created once per field and cleaned up on unmount.
  • Incoming project data no longer overwrites edits that have not been saved yet.
  • Clicking Start right after filling the form saves the pending edit first, so the backend always sees the address.
  • The places client now has timeouts (10s connect, 20s total).
